body:
## Goal

Qualify DevShard v5 and Gonka `v0.2.16` as separate, state-preserving Community DevNet changes so that a result is attributable to the component that changed.

This is an independent laboratory evaluation, not an official Gonka release or Mainnet readiness statement.

## Current status

The Community DevNet remains on Gonka `v0.2.15` and DAPI `v0.2.15-post3`.

The complete DevShard-only candidate [v2026.09.09-rc.0](https://github.com/paranjko/external-test-lab/releases/tag/v2026.09.09-rc.0) is published. Its upgrade archive and three OCI archives were independently downloaded, checked against their SHA-256 sidecars, verified with GitHub attestations, and materialized into the stable-core composition.

The candidate is not deployed. The shared public inference contract is implemented and merged, but its post-merge static-site publisher only installs static assets. It correctly failed public verification because neither the gateway-host health producer nor the public-edge proxy is installed, so the public health endpoint still exposes the preceding schema. The next operation is owner-authorized `gdc ops site` followed by `gdc ops edge`, then public API, browser, metrics, canary, and Telegram acceptance. This is not a DevShard v5 rollout. The later Gonka `v0.2.16` and hash-aware DAPI transition remains separate.

## Campaign progress

### Preparation and stable rehearsal

- [x] Publish and merge candidate lifecycle and secure build automation
- [x] Recover retained operator context without replacing validator identities
- [x] Complete the internal stable-update rehearsal with its scoped `INCONCLUSIVE` verdict
- [x] Separate core and DevShard candidate identities and add deterministic deployed-state composition contracts

### DevShard v5 update

- [x] Freeze one immutable DevShard-only candidate definition
- [x] Publish and independently verify the final DevShard v5 archive, OCI artefacts, profile, and stable-core composition
- [x] Preserve Gonka `v0.2.15` and DAPI `v0.2.15-post3` as the DevShard-only rollout baseline
- [ ] Repair and accept the shared public API, gateway, and Telegram inference-service contract
- [ ] Deploy the verified DevShard v5 candidate by controlled cohort with rollback evidence
- [ ] Run automated height-sync and residual feature packages
- [ ] Complete a paired v4/v5 functional and load comparison under equivalent working compositions
- [ ] Publish the DevShard v5 update report

### Gonka v0.2.16 and hash-aware DAPI

- [ ] Freeze and independently verify one immutable Gonka `v0.2.16` and hash-aware DAPI profile
- [ ] Complete the separate state-preserving protocol and Host-software update
- [ ] Repeat applicable v5 compatibility, height-stamp, and block-hash checks
- [ ] Publish the protocol update report

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Core and DevShard candidates have independent immutable identities
- [x] The DevShard candidate changes no Gonka core or DAPI component
- [x] Published candidate artefacts have independently verified checksums, provenance, profile, and composition
- [ ] Public inference has one truthful admission and terminal-response contract across API, site, and Telegram
- [ ] The v5 rollout proves runtime identity, consensus continuity, rollback readiness, and recovered public inference
- [ ] v4/v5 results report functional, load, quiet height-sync, busy-stamp, and residual outcomes with explicit limitations
- [ ] Public reports state the tested composition and scoped verdict without credentials or private infrastructure state

## Boundaries

- Do not reset or recreate the network to turn a failure into a pass
- Do not replace validator identities or reuse evidence from another network lineage
- Do not change core and DevShard in the same measured transition
- Do not patch official Gonka or DevShard source as a laboratory workaround
- A failed test is a result, not a reason to repeat the same cell until it passes
- A branch name, running process, container, HTTP health response, configured version, `ACTIVE` state, or one successful request is not acceptance

## Related work

- [#52](https://github.com/paranjko/external-test-lab/issues/52) is an independent public DevShard visibility follow-up. It starts after this campaign and is not part of this issue's acceptance.
